newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, blue chips to rebound.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, blue chips to rebound.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Friday with further gains among hoteliers, and traders said they expected leading issues to rebound next week after the correction.
"I think Zagrebacka Banka will move up next week. Its closing price today does not reflect the real situation," one trader said.
Zagrebacka rose six kuna to close at 1,836 after peaking at 1,865 kuna earlier on volume of 2,589 shares.

It was among seven gainers of 14 active issues in Friday's slower trade, while six stocks fell and one was flat. Volume more than halved to 11,099 shares and turnover was also lower at 8.6 million kuna.
Zagrebacka's bearer C-series jumped 70 kuna to 800, with only five shares sold. Its E-series preference stock gained 35 kuna to 1,100 and sold 249 units.
Drugs firm Pliva inched down two kuna to 470, but was the most actively traded issue with 3,245 shares sold.
"Pliva could also recover next week," the trader said, adding its current price might be too low after a correction that followed Pliva's and Zagrebacka's sudden upward thrust two weeks ago.
However, traders said there was no room for their steep rise at the moment but rather for a gradual growth.
Friday's top gainer was hotelier Riviera Porec, adding 25 kuna to 220 and selling 84 shares. Most other hotel stocks also rose.
Arenaturist edged up 10 kuna to close at 190, Jadranturist six kuna to 331 and Suncani Hvar inched up three kuna to 68.
Istraturist, which was on the rise earlier in the week, lost nine kuna on Friday to close at 250 on volume of 472 units. Laguna was also among decliners, down 10 kuna to 1,490.
"Tourist firms are poised for further growth. They are cheap and people believe they could prove lucrative if the summer season is successful," the trader said.
Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf led the decliners, losing 890 kuna to 9,000, with 22 units sold.
Food processor Podravka inched down five kuna to 350 on volume of 2,108 shares. Analysts expected it to fluctuate around its current price.
Confectioner Kras fell 24 kuna to 455. Insurer Croatia Osiguranje's B-series traded flat at 1,500 kuna.
